+title: '[MultiTool] runCode envelope: waitSeconds and timeout; outer elevation composes'
+---
+Repo: this repo. Basis: eventplan.md §"The constraint boundary, and the escape hatch" and §"The sandbox globals" (suspended-context guards).
+
+## What
+- `MultiTool.swift` `RunCodeArguments` (today: only `code`) gains the explicit control surface, each with `@Guide` documentation and token constraints:
+  - `waitSeconds` — first clock: how long this run blocks before it elevates; default the configured 5; `0` detaches immediately.
+  - `timeout` — second clock: hard limit on the work; progress resets it.
+- Outer elevation composition: Router's native mount wraps `MultiTool` in `ElevatingTool` like any tool; the engine reads the envelope's per-call `waitSeconds`/`timeout` (this consumes the sourcing seam built in the engine task). A snippet that runs past `waitSeconds` elevates while its inner promises stay in flight: the pending items are the promise plus a suspended JSC context; call settlements and elicitation answers keep resolving until the snippet ends in its terminal event. There is exactly one elevation point — no snippet ever branches on a pending envelope mid-code; inner calls never elevate.
+- Two guards on suspended contexts: a `MultiToolConfiguration` cap on live suspended JSC contexts (exceeding it is a repairable in-band error), and the hard unblock — `cancel(completionToken)` and the session-end sweep reject each pending promise, drain the microtask queue, and remove the context within the time limit (extends the existing cancellation-mid-snippet guarantee; wire the interpreter's pending-promise rejection into the mailbox canceler for the outer run).
+- `MultiToolConfiguration.executionTimeLimit`'s relationship to `timeout` must be reconciled (the watchdog enforces the interpreter limit; the envelope `timeout` is the work clock) — document the mapping in the config doc comment.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] `runCode` schema exposes `code`, `waitSeconds`, `timeout` with @Guide docs; decode of `{code}` alone still works (defaults apply)
+- [ ] A snippet exceeding `waitSeconds` (via Router-mounted ElevatingTool) yields the pending envelope while an inner fixture call is still in flight, then settles into exactly one terminal event carrying the snippet's result
+- [ ] `waitSeconds: 0` detaches immediately; the suspended-context cap triggers a repairable error, not a crash
+- [ ] `cancel(completionToken)` on a suspended snippet rejects its pending promises and tears down the context within the time limit
+- [ ] `swift test` green
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] Extend `MultiToolExecutionTests` + new suspended-context tests: schema/default decode; elevate-while-inner-in-flight settlement; zero-wait detach; cap enforcement; cancel-unblocks-context (bounded-time assertion)
+- [ ] `swift test` green
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass. #phase-1
\ No newline at end of file

 assignees:

+comments:
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01kzbmx3qshpxvpyz7kqk17tka
+  text: |-
+    Picked up; research done (explore pass over MultiTool, JSCInterpreter, RunBinding, MultiTool+SandboxGlobals, and the resolved Router's ElevatingTool/ToolElevation/ToolOutputCapping).
+
+    Findings that shape the implementation:
+
+    1. **Composition order is favorable.** `ToolOutputCapping.sessionMounted` elevates *innermost* (`ElevatingTool` directly wraps the tool, capping goes outside), so `ElevatingTool.perCallClocks`' `wrapped as? any ElevationParameterProviding` sees `MultiTool` itself. Conforming `MultiTool` is enough — no decorator-piercing needed.
+
+    2. **The watchdog reconciliation, decided.** The elevation engine already reaches the JSC watchdog: engine timeout -> `workTask.cancel()` -> `MultiTool.run`'s `withTaskCancellationHandler` -> `cancelledBox` -> `WatchdogState.isCancelled` -> terminate (~20ms poll). So the envelope `timeout` is enforced by the engine, *with* its progress resets, and the interpreter's own `timeLimit` must be the **ceiling** rather than a second, shorter clock. Arming the watchdog at the effective per-call timeout instead would silently defeat the engine's progress-reset (a heartbeat snippet would die at the un-reset value), so: watchdog := `configuration.executionTimeLimit` (the ceiling), and `elevationClocks` returns `min(envelope timeout ?? ceiling, ceiling)` so the engine's clock can never be set above the watchdog's. `executionTimeLimit`'s default rises from 5.0 to `ElevationConfiguration.defaultTimeoutSeconds` (120) — a single definition, no drift — which is what actually removes the 5s-vs-5s collision.
+
+    3. **The serial interpreter queue blocks composition.** `JSCInterpreter` holds one serial `DispatchQueue` and every `run` is a `queue.sync` on it, so a second `runCode` (the follow-up snippet that calls `wait()`/`cancel()` on a parked token) stalls behind the suspended run instead of running. Everything `evaluate` touches is per-run (its own `JSContextGroup`), so the fix is a fresh serial queue per run. That is also what makes the card's "cap on live suspended JSC contexts" meaningful — and the cap is what bounds the blocked global-queue worker threads a live context each holds.
+
+    4. **cancel() needs wiring, not reinvention.** `cancel(completionToken)` -> `mailbox.cancel` -> `ElevatingTool`'s parked canceler (`cancellationFlag.request()` + `workTask.cancel()`) -> the same cancellation path as (2) -> `pumpUntilSettled` -> `PromiseRegistry.cancelAllPending()` -> `sandbox.tearDown()`. `cancelAllPending` deliberately cancels the backing `Task`s rather than calling `resolve`/`reject` (documented safety narrowing recorded on 01KZ6MYJSSSF41HXMC2YAHBKG5 — settling would resume JS outside the watchdog's re-armed window). The card's "reject each pending promise" is satisfied observably: the awaits never resume and the context is destroyed within the time limit. Honoring the earlier human-resolved decision rather than re-opening it.
